Reaction: Diels-Alder Cycloaddition
Class: Pericyclic [4+2] concerted cycloaddition
Participants: A conjugated diene (4 π electrons, must achieve s-cis conformation) and a dienophile (2 π electrons, typically substituted with electron-withdrawing groups like C=O or CN).
title: Diels-Alder Cycloaddition [4+2] Reaction
source: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis

metadata.author: ChemNova Scientific Team
metadata.provenance: Verified Peer-Reviewed Scientific Literature / Open Chemistry Data

content:
Mechanism: Concerted single-step reaction passing through an aromatic 6-electron transition state. Forms two new carbon-carbon σ bonds and one new π bond simultaneously.
Stereospecificity: Stereospecific suprafacial-suprafacial addition; cis/trans geometry of dienophile is preserved.
Endo Rule: Secondary orbital overlap between diene and dienophile activating group stabilizes the endo transition state, favoring the endo isomer as the kinetic product.
Nobel Prize: Awarded to Otto Diels and Kurt Alder in 1950.
title: Diels-Alder Cycloaddition [4+2] Reaction
source: Strategic Applications of Named Reactions in Organic Synthesis

content:
Topic: Chemical Thermodynamics & Spontaneity
Equation: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS
where ΔG is Gibbs free energy change, ΔH is enthalpy change, T is absolute temperature (Kelvin), and ΔS is entropy change.
Spontaneity Criteria at Constant T and P:
- ΔG 0: Endergonic, non-spontaneous in the forward direction (spontaneous in reverse).
Relationship with Equilibrium Constant (Keq):
ΔG° = -R * T * ln(Keq), where R = 8.314 J/(mol·K).
When Keq > 1, ΔG° 0 (reactants favored at equilibrium).
Temperature Dependence: Governed by the Van 't Hoff equation: d(ln K)/dT = ΔH° / (R * T2).
title: Gibbs Free Energy and Chemical Equilibrium Thermodynamics
source: Atkins' Physical Chemistry (11th Edition)

metadata.author: ChemNova Scientific Team
metadata.provenance: Verified Peer-Reviewed Scientific Literature / Open Chemistry Data

content:
Topic: Reaction Rates and Activation Energy
Arrhenius Equation: k = A * exp(-Ea / (R * T))
where k is reaction rate constant, A is pre-exponential frequency factor, Ea is activation energy (J/mol), R = 8.314 J/(mol·K) is gas constant, and T is temperature in Kelvin.
Linear Form: ln(k) = ln(A) - (Ea / R) * (1 / T).
Plotting ln(k) versus (1/T) yields a straight line with slope = -Ea/R and y-intercept = ln(A).
Rule of Thumb: For many biological and organic reactions near room temperature (~300 K), a 10 °C temperature increase roughly doubles the reaction rate (Q10 coefficient ~ 2).
title: Arrhenius Equation and Chemical Reaction Kinetics
source: Levine's Physical Chemistry / IUPAC Gold Book

- 3000 - 3100 cm−1 (medium): Aromatic and Alkene =C-H stretch (sp2 hybridized).
- 2850 - 2960 cm−1 (strong): Aliphatic Alkane C-H stretch (sp3 hybridized).

* Amides: 1640 - 1690 cm−1

Topic: Inorganic Coordination Chemistry & Crystal Field Theory (CFT)
Principles: Describes electrostatic interaction between transition metal cation d-orbitals and electron-pair donor ligands modeled as point negative charges.
title: Crystal Field Theory and d-Orbital Splitting in Coordination Complexes
source: Miessler & Tarr's Inorganic Chemistry (5th Edition)

metadata.author: ChemNova Scientific Team
metadata.provenance: Verified Peer-Reviewed Scientific Literature / Open Chemistry Data

content:
Octahedral Complexes: Degenerate five d-orbitals split into two energy levels separated by crystal field splitting energy Δo (10 Dq):
- Lower energy t2g set (dxy, dyz, dxz): Orbitals point between ligand axes, minimizing electron repulsion.
- Higher energy eg set (dx2-y2, dz2): Orbitals point directly along x, y, z axes towards ligands, maximizing repulsion.
title: Crystal Field Theory and d-Orbital Splitting in Coordination Complexes
source: Miessler & Tarr's Inorganic Chemistry (5th Edition)

metadata.author: ChemNova Scientific Team
metadata.provenance: Verified Peer-Reviewed Scientific Literature / Open Chemistry Data

content:
Spectrochemical Series (Ligand field strength increasing -> larger Δo):
I− < Br− < S2− < SCN− < Cl− < F− < OH− < C2O42− < H2O < NCS− < NH3 < en < bipy < NO2− < PPh3 < CN− < CO. High Spin vs Low Spin: Strong-field ligands (e.g. CN−, CO) produce large Δo exceeding electron pairing energy (P), forcing electrons to pair in t2g (low spin, diamagnetic or reduced paramagnetism).
title: Crystal Field Theory and d-Orbital Splitting in Coordination Complexes
source: Miessler & Tarr's Inorganic Chemistry (5th Edition)
